tool_input.message:
Fixed. Committed as ff258a2 on fix/cluster2-mission-layers (on top of your pushed 3c302be) — not pushed.

**I1** — internal/mission/store.go, conflictScanIDs' doc comment (both the ~1853 ownership-mechanism line and the ~1873 cost paragraph). Both now say repoMissionIDs scans sealed audit chunks, the frozen legacy audit.jsonl, and the live not-yet-sealed tail under both repoRoot and auditRoot()'s checkoutRoot — pointing to repoMissionIDs' own doc comment in migrate.go (which was already fully accurate) for the three-source breakdown, rather than re-deriving it and risking a second drift.

**I2** — internal/mission/syncdir_unix.go: renamed the referenced test to `TestWriteContractFile_SyncDirFailureIsWarnedNotErrored` and added a line stating the current contract explicitly (rename this follows is the commit point; syncDir failure warns, doesn't error) so the comment doesn't just fix the dangling name but also states the behavior a reader would otherwise have to go find the test to learn.

**Sweep result — one more found, not "nothing else":** internal/mission/log_test.go had a leftover half-deleted doc comment. A prior edit had replaced `TestLoadEvents_FollowsSymlink_KnownWeaknessMatchesStoreLoad` (which documented symlink-following as a deliberately-carried weakness) with `TestLoadEvents_RejectsSymlink` (which asserts the opposite — LoadEvents now refuses the symlink, per ethos-jjm), but only partially deleted the old comment: it trailed off mid-sentence ("This test pins the current behavior so the follow-up is an") straight into the new test's doc comment. Worse than a dangling name — it asserted the pre-fix behavior right where a reader would look to learn the current one. `git log -S` traces it to PR #209, predating PR #508 entirely — not part of the round 2-4 diff you asked me to sweep, but the exact same defect class, so I fixed it rather than filing it as "found but left alone."

**Swept and found clean:**
- Every comment in the round 2/3/4 diff (store.go, store_test.go, migrate.go, migrate_test.go, syncdir_unix.go, syncdir_windows.go) mentioning repoMissionIDs, syncDir, writeContract, or the lock unification (withAbandonDelegationLock, missingRepoTreeDir, abandonAfterZeroCountHook) — all match current behavior. Store.Close's own delegation sweep still has its own `missingRepoTreeDir` fast path with a documented unlocked-fallback-on-lock-failure warning, which is a different, pre-existing, correctly-documented code path — not what F1/F3 fixed (that was Abandon's `withAbandonDelegationLock`, which now acquires unconditionally, matching its comment exactly).
- Every Test* name referenced anywhere in those six files resolves to a real function — checked programmatically (extracted every `Test[A-Za-z0-9_]+` token from each file, grepped for its `func` definition across the package).
- **DES-075 in DESIGN.md** — deliberately left alone. Its round-2 (F2, F4) amendment text uses round-2-accurate language ("scans audit.jsonl", "TestWriteContractFile_SyncDirFailurePropagates") describing what was true at that round; the round-3 amendment (G1 for the scan, G2/G3 for the sync contract) explicitly documents both corrections — G2/G3 even names the exact rename ("`TestWriteContractFile_SyncDirFailureIsWarnedNotErrored` (renamed from round 2's `..._SyncDirFailurePropagates`...)"). ADR amendments are sequential historical narrative, each one correcting the last on the record — that's a different contract than a live code comment describing current behavior, so no edit needed there.

Comment-only diff, no behavior change, no new tests (per your note).

**Gates:**
- `make check`: green.
- `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...`: exit 0.
- Detached gate: 27 ok / 0 FAIL / 1 no-test-files — matches expected.

Files: internal/mission/store.go, internal/mission/syncdir_unix.go, internal/mission/log_test.go

Fixed in `ff258a2`. Worse than a dangling name, which is why it was worth more than a rename.

The old name — `...SyncDirFailurePropagates` — asserts the *opposite* of the current contract. Round 3 changed `writeContract` so a `syncDir` failure is warned to stderr and returns nil, because the rename it follows is the commit point: `dest` already holds the correct, complete contract regardless of what the directory fsync reports. A reader trusting the comment would conclude a failed fsync aborts the write, and might "restore" error propagation — reintroducing the failure mode round 3 removed.

So the fix names the current test *and* states the contract inline, rather than leaving the reader to infer durability semantics from a test name.

Also swept the rest of the round-2/3/4 diff for the same class rather than waiting to be told about a third. That turned up one more, outside this PR's diff: `log_test.go` carried a half-deleted doc comment from #209 explaining that `LoadEvents` deliberately *follows* symlinks as a known carried weakness — trailing off mid-sentence directly into the doc comment for its replacement, `TestLoadEvents_RejectsSymlink`, which asserts it refuses to. Two contradictory descriptions fused into one block above a test that does the second thing. Pre-existing, not ours, fixed anyway.

`DESIGN.md` checked and deliberately left alone: DES-075's round-2 text is round-2-accurate and its round-3 amendment names this very rename. ADR amendments are a historical record of what was decided when — rewriting them to match current code would destroy the thing they exist to preserve. Different rule than for code comments, which must describe the code as it is now.

tool_input.message:
Round 7 on PR #508, one finding, and it's a defect the round-6 fix introduced — I approved it, so this one is on me, not you.

**J1 — `internal/mission/store.go` ~1856 (and check the cost paragraph at ~1873 for the same error).** The new comment says the live not-yet-sealed tail lives under `<repoRoot>/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/`. It does not. I traced it: `collectLiveContractIDs` → `audit.LiveSessionsDir(root)` → `LocalZoneBase(root)` = `<root>/.punt-labs/local/ethos/sessions/`.

So the three sources are in two different zones, and the comment now names one path for all three:

- sealed chunks + frozen legacy `audit.jsonl` → `<repoRoot>/.punt-labs/ethos/sessions/<session>/` — git-tracked
- live tail → `<root>/.punt-labs/local/ethos/sessions/` — gitignored, machine-local, scanned under both `repoRoot` and `checkoutRoot`

That's the DES-058 two-zone split, and `internal/audit/paths.go:20-24` states it explicitly.

Fix the comment to name both zones distinctly, and say which is tracked and which is machine-local — that property is the whole reason the worktree bug in round 4 existed, and a reader who thinks the live tail is tracked will not understand why a linked worktree needed a second root at all.

Check the cost paragraph too; if it inherited the same single-path framing, fix it there as well.

Worth naming the pattern, because it is the third time this exact distinction has bitten this PR: round 3 was the sealed-chunk blind spot, round 4 was the live-tail-under-checkoutRoot blind spot, and now round 7 is a comment that erases the boundary between them. The two-zone split is the hard part of this code, and prose about it needs the same scrutiny as the code. When you fix the comment, make the zone boundary the thing the comment is *about*, not an incidental detail in a path string — that is what makes the next reader get it right.

Same drill: `make check`, `GOOS=windows GOARCH=amd64 go build ./...` exit 0, detached gate (report `ok` and `FAIL` counts), commit, do not push.
